claim_one_line: THE STALE-CLAIM GATE, and the sweep that says the class has exactly one member. B1181 was retracted by B1235 on 2026-09-02 ('the family is 38/112 amphichiral, not 83/83') and THE PAPER carried the retracted sentence for a week regardless; no gate caught it, because the arc-verdict gate checks shape not currency, the harvest gate tracks seat debt not claim staleness, and THE PAPER deliberately names no internal identifiers, so any gate keyed on arc IDs is blind by construction. THE SWEEP: of 12 RETRACTED arcs and 46 with superseded_by, exactly ONE carries a populated retracted-by block written by another arc -- B1181. The other three RETRACTED arcs flagged by an ID-based scan (B964, B731, B519) are FALSE POSITIVES: each is a self-correcting arc whose claim_one_line IS the correction, and the live documents cite the corrected content. So the error class is closed at one member and THE PAPER is not carrying others. THE INSTRUMENT: a retraction may now declare retracted.stale_phrases -- the wordings that must not speak unqualified again -- and tests/test_b1326_retracted_claims_do_not_speak.py enforces it against ten live documents, requiring a retraction marker within 400 characters. The matcher normalises LaTeX ($, braces, emph/textbf wrappers) and PDF ligatures, WITHOUT WHICH IT DOES NOT WORK: the first version missed the historical defect entirely because the paper reads 'all $83$ members', and a gate that cannot see through the markup of the document it guards is vacuous. VALIDATED AGAINST HISTORY: run on main.tex at b94ed03 the gate fires on B1181 twice; run on the corrected paper it is clean; and a bite control proves it fires on a planted unqualified claim and stays silent on a properly qualified one.
